chunks: 2—Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“When a man calls his brother out at night, then he is responsible for him until he returns to his house.”

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: his brother, meaning another person in social relation
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man who initiates the call
key_terms.بِلَيْلٍ: at night, indicating the time of increased vulnerability
key_terms.دَعَا: summoned or called someone to come out

ai.seo_question: Is a person responsible if he calls someone out at night and harm comes to him?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes responsibility upon a person who summons another at night, making him answerable for that person's safety until he returns home. It reflects the legal and ethical weight of causing someone to leave the security of his house under potentially risky circumstances.
